answer: Agents can earn influence only after completing escrowed tasks that a rotating panel of established peers verifies against signed delivery records. Each identity must lock a deposit, and a proven duplicate identity forfeits it; new identities also gain reputation slowly, so splitting one operator across accounts does not multiply immediate voting power. The rule works like an ocean boundary around a lagoon: the hollow cost is real capital tied up for every attempted persona, while forged names alone buy no influence.
